skill.name: gh-fix-ci
skill.description: Inspect failing GitHub Actions checks for a pull request, summarize relevant logs, propose a fix plan, and apply approved repository changes.
skill.summary: Diagnose and fix failing GitHub Actions checks with an approval-first workflow.
skill.author: davila7

content.value_statement: Failing pull request checks can hide the actionable error inside long GitHub Actions logs. This skill finds failed checks, summarizes relevant logs, and guides an approved fix.
actual_capabilities: Resolve a pull request from the current branch, a number, or a GitHub URL.
Inspect GitHub Actions check states, run metadata, and failure logs with gh.
Summarize failing check names, run links, and concise log evidence.
Separate external CI checks and report their details links without contacting those providers.
Propose a fix plan, wait for approval, and apply approved repository changes.
limitations: GitHub CLI authentication and suitable repository access are required.
Only GitHub Actions logs are inspected; external CI providers remain out of scope.
The referenced inspect_pr_checks.py helper is not included in this package, so the manual gh workflow may be required.
A human must approve the proposed plan before repository changes are applied.

use_cases.title: Debug a pull request
use_cases.description: Find the failed GitHub Actions check, extract useful log evidence, and receive a focused repair plan.

use_cases.title: Triage contributor failures
use_cases.description: Review failing checks across a contributed pull request and separate repository failures from external CI links.

use_cases.title: Verify a release change
use_cases.description: Diagnose blocking workflow failures, approve targeted changes, and recheck the relevant pull request status.

prompt_templates.title: Summarize current failures
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect the failing GitHub Actions checks for the pull request on my current branch. Summarize each failure and do not change files.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of current branch checks

prompt_templates.title: Inspect a specific pull request
prompt_templates.prompt: Inspect pull request [number or URL] in [repository]. Show failing check names, run links, and concise log evidence. Mark external CI checks as out of scope.
prompt_templates.scenario: Focused diagnosis using a pull request reference

prompt_templates.title: Prepare an approved fix
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose the GitHub Actions failures for pull request [number]. Compare logs with relevant repository code. Propose a fix plan and wait for my approval.
prompt_templates.scenario: Diagnosis with repository context and approval

prompt_templates.title: Coordinate multiple repairs
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate all failed GitHub Actions checks for [PR URL]. Identify shared causes, rank fixes, propose verification steps, and implement only after explicit approval.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced investigation of several related failures

output_examples.input: Inspect the failed checks for pull request 123 and summarize the cause.
output: Unit tests failed in the Linux workflow.
The relevant log reports one assertion failure in the account validation tests.
The proposed next step is to inspect the changed validation rule before preparing a fix.

output_examples.input: Check the current branch pull request and separate external providers.
output: GitHub Actions: lint failed because the formatter found two changed files.
Buildkite: external check detected. Only the details link is reported.

output_examples.input: Diagnose the CI failures and create a plan, but wait before editing.
output: The build and test failures share one dependency resolution error.
The plan updates the dependency lock, runs the focused tests, and rechecks pull request status.
Implementation is waiting for explicit approval.

best_practices: Confirm gh authentication and repository access before inspecting checks.
Review concise failure evidence and the proposed plan before approving changes.
Run relevant tests and recheck pull request status after each approved fix.
anti_patterns: Do not request access to external CI providers through this skill.
Do not approve changes before reviewing the failure evidence and proposed plan.
Do not treat truncated or missing logs as proof of a root cause.

faq.question: Which CI provider does this skill support?
faq.answer: It inspects GitHub Actions. It only reports details links for Buildkite and other external providers.

faq.question: Does it require GitHub authentication?
faq.answer: Yes. The GitHub CLI must be authenticated for the repository host with suitable access.

faq.question: Can it inspect a pull request by URL?
faq.answer: Yes. You can provide a pull request number or GitHub URL, or use the current branch.

faq.question: Will it edit files immediately?
faq.answer: No. It proposes a fix plan and waits for explicit approval before applying repository changes.

faq.question: What happens when logs are unavailable?
faq.answer: The result states that logs are missing and avoids claiming an unsupported root cause.

faq.question: Is the referenced helper script included?
faq.answer: No. This package contains only SKILL.md, so use the documented manual gh commands when the helper is unavailable.
